belief: The side effects prove nothing will ever work for me.
origins: Nausea, drowsiness, weight change, or other effects can make us want to quit. After a bad experience with one medication, we may assume all treatments will fail or be intolerable.
teaches: Scripture counsels wisdom and counsel: “Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.” “Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.” Side effects are real and deserve a doctor’s attention. They do not mean that no option exists. Doctors can often adjust dose, timing, or type. God works through persistent, honest conversation and wise adjustments.
self_statements: I will never find something that works.
The cure is worse than the illness.
errors: Believing a treatment is either perfect or useless.
Predicting that no medicine will work.
Feeling sick and concluding that nothing can help.
questions: What exactly are the side effects, and how bad are they?
Have I told my doctor or pharmacist?
How long did I give it, and what did the doctor advise?
What would help me cope with side effects in the meantime?
Who can help me track what happens?
truth: Side effects are real and worth addressing, but they do not prove that nothing will work. I can talk with my doctor, adjust or switch under supervision, and keep trusting God for wisdom.
log: Each week, note one conversation with your care team and its result.
actions: Look to the Lord for help.
prayer: Lord, this treatment is hard on me. Give wisdom to my doctors, patience to me, and hope that there is a path forward. Amen.
